historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 90 2.2 TDCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.2 TDCi "Puma" engine was introduced to the Defender 90, it marked the final evolution of the classic Defender lineage, bringing Euro 5 compliance and refined Ford-sourced Duratorq technology to the iconic short-wheelbase off-roader.

milestones.description: DT224 (2.2L TDCi), 122hp, introduced to replace the 2.4 TDCi, featuring a revised turbocharger, EGR system, and Euro 5 emissions compliance.
End of classic Defender 90 2.2 TDCi production, concluding the lineage before the modern L663 generation launch.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Land Rover Defender 90 2.2 TDCi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h3: The Land Rover Defender 90 2.2 TDCi (DT224) is generally robust, but as a high-mileage workhorse, it is susceptible to specific wear points. Rebuilt engines sourced through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbo Actuator & Wastegate Failure - Why the Land Rover Defender 90 2.2 TDCi DT224 Loses Boost
problems.rootCause: Carbon buildup and heat stress cause the turbo wastegate actuator to stick, leading to sudden power loss or limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the faulty actuator and cleaning the wastegate mechanism.
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix if the turbo core is still healthy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call for high-mileage units or when turbo failure has caused secondary engine damage.

problems.recommendation: For minor EGR or actuator issues on a low-mileage example, targeted specialist repair is cost-effective. However, if the DT224 has suffered catastrophic turbo failure, severe oil dilution, or timing chain tensioner wear, a full rebuilt engine is the most reliable long-term solution to protect your investment.

problems.group: EGR Cooler Leaks & Injector Seal Failure
problems.h4: EGR Cooler Leaks & Injector Seal Failure - Why the Land Rover Defender 90 2.2 TDCi DT224 Suffers Carbon Buildup
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler is prone to internal leaks, allowing coolant into the intake, while failing injector seals cause severe carbon buildup around the cylinder head.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing injector seals, cleaning or blanking the EGR system, and flushing the intake.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable preventative maintenance if caught early before head damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if coolant ingestion has warped the head or caused hydrolock.
